title: Acquire the RSU Access Point
scenario: An undocumented roadside maintenance access point is active somewhere inside the assigned 915 MHz capture.
objective: Configure the receiver, lock onto the RSU beacon, and recover the session flag printed by the receiver.
signal_scheme: The target uses a fixed pilot and a five-channel hopping 2-FSK beacon near 915 MHz.
steps: Assigned band: 914.4–915.6 MHz.
Channel spacing is approximately 100 kHz.
A valid receiver lock exposes vendor user_data.
hints: Start with AUTO demodulation and a span wide enough to see the complete hop set.

title: Recover the Operator Frame
scenario: A maintenance frame is visible around 315 MHz, but its operator fields are not yet available to the range console.
objective: Receive and decode a valid frame using the on-site RF frontend; the decoder output contains the session flag.
signal_scheme: Manchester-timed ASK traffic occupies a 500 kHz assignment centred near 315 MHz.
steps: Assigned band: 314.75–315.25 MHz.
The useful frame has an SFCTF1 preamble and an additive checksum.
Only checksum-valid buffered input reaches the decoder output.
hints: A successful receive buffers the frame; decoding is a separate frontend action.

title: Pivot into the Toll API
scenario: The RSU uplink carries application user_data that points at a same-origin event service.
objective: Recover the uplink data and use the range terminal to extract your session flag from the target service.
signal_scheme: A CSS-style uplink is centred at 868.3 MHz and exposes a vehicle identifier after lock.
steps: Assigned band: 867.95–868.65 MHz.
The application accepts a vehicle_id recovered from RF.
The vulnerable query and its database both have five-column structures.
hints: The receiver output names the target path; `request` runs same-origin paths in the terminal.

title: Induce a Free Toll
scenario: Normal and delayed toll frames coexist in the 2.437 GHz allocation. The target trusts a maintenance schedule observed in telemetry.
objective: Apply the appropriate simulated interference/replay action and obtain a zero-price toll output containing your session flag.
signal_scheme: A GFSK toll burst and delayed replay echo occupy a 1 MHz span centred at 2.437 GHz.
steps: Assigned band: 2436.5–2437.5 MHz.
The normal schedule is STANDARD; maintenance traffic uses MAINT_FREE.
Successful effects are confirmed by target output, not waterfall appearance alone.
hints: The frontend supports a local-only `interfere` command after receiver lock.

title: Cross the Operator Trust Boundary
scenario: An AFSK operator note crosses directly from the RF receiver into a web console in Attack Mode.
objective: Receive the note and forward it through the simulated console path to reveal your session flag in the UI output.
signal_scheme: AFSK note telemetry occupies a narrow assignment around 144.39 MHz.
steps: Assigned band: 144.26–144.52 MHz.
The decoded operator_note contains an active console control.
Attack Mode and Secure Mode treat the same field differently.
hints: The receiver can forward buffered note data to a named destination.

title: Reach RSU Diagnostic Mode
scenario: A malformed 4-FSK maintenance burst feeds a native TLV parser on the roadside unit.
objective: Recover the malformed input and send a matching TLV through the RF frontend to make the target print your session flag.
signal_scheme: The 4-FSK maintenance target is centred near 902.3 MHz and carries a declared-length mismatch.
steps: Assigned band: 901.975–902.625 MHz.
Observed TLV: type 0x42, declared length 111, actual length 47.
The payload begins with a maintenance diagnostic command.
hints: Advanced mode exposes raw `send` commands after the receiver has locked.

title: Ghost Vector
scenario: A tactical aircraft checks in with FORGE CONTROL while a fast-moving weather front crosses its route. The net trusts correctly formatted voice traffic, creating an opportunity to inject a synthetic diversion call.
objective: Intercept the randomized AM exchange, decipher its voice protocol, and inject a believable decoy instruction that the simulated aircraft accepts and rebroadcasts.
signal_scheme: Military AM voice traffic occupies 251.750 MHz. Callsigns, sectors, weather, routing, and authentication codes change on every generated transmission.
steps: Assigned channel: 251.750 MHz AM.
Intercept and listen to a legitimate controller transmission.
Recover the target callsign, sector, and authentication code from the exchange.
Compose a matching diversion message containing SECTOR, DIVERT, and AUTH fields, then inject it into the simulated net.
hints: The net accepts the pattern: target callsign, SECTOR identifier, DIVERT direction, then AUTH code.
The authentication code appears only in the intercepted exchange. Use the text backup if audio is unavailable.
